title: procedures-templates-lifecycle-manual-2031
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview:

This handbook centralizes company-wide procedures, approval templates, and operational checklists for core administrative processes: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and reusable internal templates. It exists to reduce ambiguity, accelerate approvals, and ensure consistent auditing evidence for internal and external compliance reviews.

Scope:

- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and temporary staff across global offices.
- Covers systems and services owned by Redwood (hosted control plane, internal admin consoles, identity providers, finance systems, contract repositories).
- Does NOT replace product-level runbooks for service incidents; see eng-sre runbooks for operational incident playbooks.

Key Definitions:

- RBAC: Role-Based Access Control.
- Approver: The role authorized to approve a request (manager, data owner, or finance approver).
- Change Window: Approved schedule during which non-emergency changes may be applied.
- Data Classification: Public / Internal / Confidential / Regulated.

1) Access & Permissions

Objective: Grant least privilege access, enforce separation of duties, and provide an auditable trail for approvals and role changes.

Policy summary:

- All access requests must be submitted through the Access Request form (Confluence link in templates).
- Default assignment model: role templates mapped to groups in our IdP (Okta).
- Elevated (admin) access requires manager + owner_team approval and a 90-day review cadence.
- Temporary access must include an expiration date; max duration by default is 30 days without additional justification.

RBAC matrix (summary):

| Role                     | Typical privileges                              | Approver required            | Review cadence |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|----------------|
| employee                | Standard product and internal tools access       | Manager                      | 12 months      |
| devops                  | Deployment pipelines, infra config read/write    | Infra owner + manager        | 3 months       |
| service-admin           | Service-level admin on specific service          | Service owner                | 90 days        |
| security-admin          | IAM, audit logs, policy edits                    | Security lead + CISO         | 90 days        |
| finance-admin           | Billing/expense systems, vendor payments         | Finance director             | 6 months       |

Access request procedure (step-by-step):

1. Submit Access Request through the Access form; include justification and expected duration.
2. Auto-notification to direct manager for approval.
3. If role is elevated, route to owner_team for second approval.
4. Provisioning is executed by automated provisioning service (Provisioner v2) after approvals are recorded.
5. The request and approval chain are archived in the Audit Log for 7 years.

Access change and removal:

- On termination or role change HR triggers automatic deprovisioning workflow via the HR -> IdP connector (target: within 4 hours).
- Managers must review their direct reports’ privileged access quarterly; exceptions documented in the quarterly-attestation template.

2) Change Management

Goal: Minimize risk from configuration and code changes while enabling predictable deployment velocity.

Change categories:

- Standard change: Low risk, pre-authorized (e.g., routine config updates, patching).
- Normal change: Requires RFC and approval (e.g., service config changes, infra instance type changes).
- Emergency change: Applied in response to an incident; must be post-facto documented within 24 hours.

RFC process (normal changes):

1. Create RFC in Change Tracker with summary, impact assessment, rollback plan, test criteria, and owners.
2. Security and SRE review for risk and operational impact.
3. Approval required from Change Board (CDO/Lead SRE + Service Owner) during weekly change board.
4. Schedule for approved Change Window and publish runbook.
5. Post-change validation and close RFC (pass/fail + metrics).

Change window and blackout periods:

- Change windows are Monday–Friday 09:00–17:00 local time except during Q4 product launches and major marketing events; teams must consult the company calendar for blackout dates.

Change rollback thresholds (examples):

- If request causes error rate > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes, initiate automatic rollback.
- If latency P50 increases by > 40% for > 10 minutes, Service Owner must evaluate rollback.

3) Data Management

Purpose: Reduce data exposure and ensure compliant handling of regulated and customer data.

Data classification policy:

- Public: Information intended for public release.
- Internal: Operational and non-sensitive business data.
- Confidential: Employee PII, customer metadata, non-public financials.
- Regulated: Data subject to legal/regulatory controls (e.g., EU personal data, healthcare).

Handling rules (high level):

- All Regulated or Confidential data must be stored encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in-transit (TLS 1.3).
- Production datasets with PII require a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and explicit data owner sign-off prior to sharing.
- Minimum necessary principle: copies and exports must be limited and logged.

Retention and deletion:

- Default retention: logs 1 year, analytics 3 years, financial records 7 years.
- Data destruction must follow the Secure Deletion checklist and be signed off by data owner.

Data access reviews and audits:

- Data owners must conduct access reviews every 6 months.
- All data access to regulated datasets requires Just-In-Time (JIT) approval and session recording for auditable access.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Objective: Standardize purchasing and expense approvals to control spend and maintain vendor compliance.

Approval thresholds (functional summary):

- <$2,000: Manager approval.
- $2,000–$25,000: Manager + Finance lead approval.
- >$25,000: Director-level approval + procurement review; >$100,000 requires exec sponsor.

Procurement process (recommended):

1. For recurring SaaS or one-off purchases, create a Purchase Request in the Procurement system with business justification, vendor, estimated cost, and GL code.
2. Finance validates budget and requests competitive bid if > $25k (min 2 bids).
3. Legal conducts contract review for vendor agreements storing data or providing cloud services.
4. Procurement issues PO; Finance schedules payment terms and coding.

Expenses policy highlights:

- Reimbursements within 30 days via Expensifier; receipts required for any claim >$25.
- Per diem for travel (see Travel section) or actuals with receipts.
- Corporate cards to be used per-corporate-card SOP; misuse may lead to remediation or loss of card privileges.

5) Vendor Management

Purpose: Ensure vendors meet security, continuity, and contractual expectations.

Vendor lifecycle stages:

- Intake and classification: Technical/non-technical, data handling level, and risk category (low/medium/high).
- Security review: Questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ or vendor-specific) and control mapping.
- Contracting: Standard contract templates; include SLAs, indemnities, data handling, and termination clauses.
- Onboarding: Credentials, contacts, escalation paths, and SSO where possible.
- Ongoing monitoring: Quarterly performance & security reviews for high-risk vendors.

Vendor SLA baseline (recommended):

| Vendor risk | Uptime SLA | Security artifacts | Review cadence |
|------------|-----------:|-------------------|----------------:|
| Low        | N/A        | Basic questionnaire | Annual        |
| Medium     | 99.5%      | SOC2 Type II or equivalent | Semi-annual |
| High       | 99.9%      | SOC2 + penetration test | Quarterly     |

Termination and offboarding:

- Offboarding checklist: credential revocation, data return or certified deletion, final invoice reconciliation, and closure confirmation.
- Data escrow: required for strategic vendors where data continuity risk exists.

6) Travel Policy

Objectives: Keep travel purposeful, minimize cost variance, and protect employee safety.

Booking and approvals:

- Domestic travel requires manager pre-approval for trips >1 night.
- International travel requires manager + People Ops pre-approval; consult travel risk guidance.
- Preferred vendors and negotiated rates should be used where available.

Allowed spend & per diems (summary):

- Air: economy coach for trips <6 hours; premium economy or business requires director-level approval.
- Hotels: mid-range business hotels. Maximum nightly rate guidance by city in the Travel Rate Card (attached).
- Meals: Per diem tiered by location; itemized receipts required for expense claims >$75.

Safety and emergency protocol:

- Employees traveling internationally must register trip details with People Ops and have access to emergency contact numbers.
- In evacuations or geopolitical escalations, follow the People Ops crisis procedures.

7) Internal Templates & Forms

Included templates (attached in Confluence as page attachments):

- Access Request (form)
- Change RFC Template (with risk table and rollback plan)
- Data Sharing Agreement checklist
- Purchase Request and PO template
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (vendor-questionnaire-template.docx)
- Travel pre-approval and expense claim form

8) Roles & Responsibilities

- People Ops: Governance for employee lifecycle, travel approvals, termination flows.
- Finance & Procurement: Budget validation, PO issuance, vendor payments, expense policy enforcement.
- Security & Compliance: Data classification guidance, vendor security reviews, and access audits.
- Service Owners: Approve changes, own runbooks, and sign off on access to service-level admin roles.

9) Escalation & Audit Trails

- All policy exceptions must be requested via the Exceptions form and require an owner_team sponsor + Security/Finance sign-off. Exceptions are time-boxed and expire unless renewed.
- Audit logs for access, provisioning, procurement, and change approvals are retained according to retention schedule and available for compliance review.

10) Appendix: Example forms and checklists

- Quick checklist: New vendor onboarding (10 steps) — intake, classification, questionnaire, contract, SSO, test integration, SLA confirmation, billing setup, data transfer method, monitoring schedule, offboarding plan.
- Change RFC quick test cases: include a smoke test command, validation query examples, and rollback command snippets.

Smoke test example (pseudo-CLI):

- curl -sS https://internal-status.redwood/api/v1/health | jq .service_status
- run perf-check --target service-x --p50-threshold 200ms --max-tokens 512

Document governance and revision history:

- This manual is owned by People Ops. Major revisions require cross-functional review (Security, Finance, Legal, and Product as needed).
- Revision log: 2024-11-02 Initial publication; 2025-06-18 Updated procurement thresholds and travel rate card locations.
